name: Saves the Day
label: Equal Vision
lede: A New Jersey high school band wrote the blueprint for a decade of emo and pop-punk, partly in an NYU psychology class. They survived a van wreck and a major label that dropped them days after their album came out, and Chris Conley outlasted more than a dozen bandmates.

eras.title: A Jersey high school band picks a new name
eras.text: A New Jersey band called Sefler played melodic hardcore through high school, renamed itself, and made a debut album on winter break. Equal Vision put it out the summer they graduated, and touring it cost the band most of its members.

years.h: Sefler starts in New Jersey, with Chris Conley on bass and vocals
years.p: The band that becomes Saves the Day begins as a four-piece playing melodic hardcore, with Conley singing and playing bass.

years.h: Sean McGrath looks at Sefler and comes up with Saves the Day
years.p: The bassist supplies the new name. Conley and drummer Bryan Newman are the constants.

years.h: Over a winter break, a high school band records Can't Slow Down
years.p: Producer Steve Evetts has them in the studio during Conley's senior-year break, with the band still in school.

years.h: Can't Slow Down · Equal Vision EVR 42
years.p: McGrath borrowed the title from a 1983 Lionel Richie album. The melodic hardcore debut had sold 8,000 copies by the time its follow-up came out.

years.h: Boston hardcore band [[Bane|adf5ac61-4d7b-4cbc-95ce-ee2dc486f884]] takes them on their first full US tour
years.p: It's Saves the Day's first full tour of the United States.

years.h: The van driver and the roadie both end up in the band
years.p: Guitarist Justin Gaylord quits after the first tour. David Soloway, who used to drive the band around in high school, takes his place, and roadie Ted Alexander is simply handed a guitar.
years.xp: McGrath, the only bassist on Can't Slow Down, was pushed out while the next album was being written. Conley heard Eben D'Amico in a local band and brought him in.

eras.title: Written in Psychology 101
eras.text: Conley wrote Through Being Cool at NYU, and Equal Vision's staff couldn't stop playing it. The band dropped out of college to tour it, and it sold like nothing the label had seen. Then the van crashed.

years.h: 500 copies of I'm Sorry I'm Leaving, acoustic, on Immigrant Sun
years.p: An Equal Vision employee asked for an acoustic record after hearing "Three Miles Down." The EP comes out in mid-1999.

years.h: Eleven days in South River, and Conley's voice quits before the record does
years.p: The band records Through Being Cool with Evetts at Trax East, pulling all-nighters. Two extra half-days get booked to finish the vocals.
years.xp:
Newman came close to a breakdown in the studio and called Evetts "definitely the guru of the whole thing." Conley called the sessions "just having a blast."

His listening that summer: the Foo Fighters' The Colour and the Shape, Weezer's Pinkerton and Joni Mitchell's Blue.

years.cap: Saves the Day at the Karma Club, Boston, August 15, 1999
q: the most important record that we did
years.h: Conley writes Through Being Cool in lecture halls
years.p: Lyrics in Psychology 101 at NYU, guitar parts at Newman's apartment on 7th Street and 2nd Avenue. Equal Vision releases it as EVR-54.
years.xp:
The songs were refined in Conley's parents' basement, with the band working all weekend. Alternative Press named it one of its ten most influential albums of 1999, and later argued it shaped [[Fall Out Boy|516cef4d-0718-4007-9939-f9b38af3f784]], [[My Chemical Romance|c07f0676-9143-4217-8a9f-4c26bd636f13]] and [[Taking Back Sunday|350bce49-c21b-4137-b50a-0766ded07e4d]].

Patrick Stump of Fall Out Boy: "I would not have been in Fall Out Boy if it weren't for this record." The release show was with [[The Get Up Kids|1b54e90c-638e-4fdd-a20e-4ab09db9fdaf]], [[At the Drive-In|7e13cd1c-0300-4d03-bd8e-5f86dd99d74f]] and Midtown.

years.big: "Look at the album cover; you guys are selling out."
years.h: Hardcore kids read the glossy cover as a sellout
years.p: Conley recalls the reaction to the photo of the five members as outcasts on a couch at a high school party. In the hardcore world of 1999, faces on the sleeve meant rock star.
years.xp: Equal Vision's Dan Sandshaw had worried the cover sent the wrong message, and Newman regretted it. The CD art shows [[Gabe Saporta|8f4ad807-3363-46d1-8b2a-93a02fe6eb22]] kissing his college girlfriend, and actor James Ransone is passed out on a couch on the back.

years.cap: Saves the Day on stage, July 2000
years.h: The van crashes on the H2O tour, and the band almost doesn't survive it
years.p: It happens on a March-to-May 2000 North American run with [[H2O|b4307812-8143-46e0-9075-ffc06b30f3fe]]. The band rejoins the tour in Seattle.
years.xp: Wikipedia's Through Being Cool page says only that the crash "almost ended their career." The location and any injuries aren't in the sources used here.

years.h: Soloway's parents' house stars in a video the band hated
years.p: Director Darren Doan shoots "Shoulder to the Wheel" there in February with friends of the band, and it goes to stations April 7. Newman says they hated it as soon as they saw it.
years.xp: The band mimed to the song after playing other tracks to set the mood.

years.h: Through Being Cool nears 50,000, and Vagrant comes calling
years.p: That's a huge number for Equal Vision. Saves the Day sign to Vagrant Records, and founder Rich Egan becomes their manager.
years.xp: Egan "fell in love" with the band, Wikipedia says, because the lyrics were "so honest, so cut and dried."

eras.title: A major label gives up in three days
eras.text: On Vagrant, Saves the Day got on late-night TV, opened for Weezer and Blink-182 and made a video with Muppet-style puppets. Then DreamWorks released In Reverie and walked away within days.

years.h: Stay What You Are sells 14,970 in its first week
years.p: Rob Schnapf produces in Hollywood. By March 2002 it passes 120,000, and "At Your Funeral" and "Freakish" land on MTV2.

years.h: The last founding member besides Conley goes back to school
years.p: Drummer Bryan Newman leaves for college, and Damon Atkinson of Hey Mercedes fills in.

years.h: Conan first, then Weezer's Hyper Extended Midget Tour
years.p: After a December spot on The Late Late Show, Saves the Day play Late Night with Conan O'Brien and join the tour.

years.h: Muppet-style puppets replace the band in the "Freakish" video
years.p: The band then spends May and June on the Pop Disaster Tour with [[Blink-182|0743b15a-3c32-48c8-ad58-cb325350befa]] and [[Green Day|084308bd-1654-436f-ba03-df6697104e19]].

years.h: "At Your Funeral" climbs to No. 76 in Britain
years.p: Saves the Day are over there supporting [[Alkaline Trio|69421e11-e4c3-4854-951b-ceab4972e38e]].

years.h: Roadie turned guitarist Ted Alexander is fired
years.p: Alexander, handed a guitar in 1998, is dismissed, and Conley takes over guitar. Pete Parada becomes the drummer.

years.big: "DreamWorks Records completely abandoned it three days after it was released."
q: saying that we made the wrong record
years.src: Wikipedia: In Reverie · Wikipedia: Saves the Day
years.h: DreamWorks walks away from In Reverie within days
years.p: The album enters the Billboard 200 at No. 27 on 34,000 first-week copies. Interscope then absorbs DreamWorks and drops the band.
years.xp:
Rob Schnapf produced it. Conley's account is that DreamWorks said Saves the Day had made the wrong record. After the band's largest headlining show, the DreamWorks A&R contact told him: "None of the programmers at radio are biting at the single, and MTV doesn't want to play the video."

Interscope staff declined to engage and paid the band severance to leave. The album kept selling, 150,000 by mid-2006, and scored 77 on Metacritic, an A- from Entertainment Weekly and a C+ from Spin.

years.h: Sean McGrath, who named the band, dies at 28
years.p: He played on Can't Slow Down and died of intestinal cancer after a two-year illness. Vagrant's B-sides collection Ups and Downs is dedicated to him.

years.cap: Chris Conley at Campus Philly, Philadelphia, September 29, 2006
years.h: With no label, Conley builds a studio in Chico
years.p: The Electric Ladybug, in Chico, California, becomes his home studio and where later records get cut.

eras.title: The trilogy
eras.text: Conley wrote three albums as one arc, discontent, remorse, acceptance, and called it a therapeutic experiment. By the end, no one but Conley had played on an earlier Saves the Day record.

years.h: Sound the Alarm opens the trilogy with discontent
years.p: Recorded in 2005 with no label, the fifth album comes out after Saves the Day re-sign with Vagrant in January.

years.h: Pete Parada leaves for [[The Offspring|23a03e33-a603-404e-bcbf-2c00159d7067]]
years.p: After more than four years, he goes. Durijah Lang of [[Glassjaw|429f9fbf-0a0b-4a9e-a88c-94d48aa466ed]] takes the drums and plays on Under the Boards.

years.h: Under the Boards takes on reflection and remorse
years.p: Part two of the trilogy, released on Vagrant.

years.cap: Chris Conley and David Soloway, Salt Lake City, April 19, 2007
years.h: Conley and Soloway team up with Max Bemis as [[Two Tongues|85bcd622-bad8-4dd7-b577-ff7f5c195852]]
years.p: Bemis and drummer Coby Linder of [[Say Anything|ee90d1b3-a4e2-4d18-9092-111d856e7e7a]] complete the band. The self-titled album, cut at the Electric Ladybug, comes out in February.

years.h: Arun Bali takes lead guitar after David Soloway's decade-plus run
years.p: Soloway departs in March, and Bali replaces him in April.

years.h: The rhythm section goes back to Glassjaw
years.p: Bassist Manuel Carrero and drummer Durijah Lang leave. Rodrigo Palma takes bass and Spencer Peterson the drums.
years.xp: Peterson lasted until September 2010, when he left to join Black Cards, [[Pete Wentz|26cea341-dfab-483f-9cdb-8de82da81019]]'s electropop project. Claudio Rivera replaced him.

years.h: Daybreak ends the trilogy on Razor & Tie
years.p: After several delays, the acceptance chapter arrives. It's the first Saves the Day album on which no one but Conley had played on an earlier record.

eras.title: Back to Equal Vision
eras.text: Saves the Day went direct to fans to fund the next record, toured Through Being Cool for its fifteenth birthday, and in 2018 made their ninth album for the label that started them.

years.h: Fans pay for the eighth album through PledgeMusic
years.p: Pledgers get demos of "Ain't No Kind of Love" and a Christmas cover of "Baby Please Come Home."

years.h: Dennis Wilson takes over from Claudio Rivera on drums
years.p: Rivera had held the seat since 2010.

years.cap: Saves the Day at Tress, Dallas, October 10, 2013
years.h: The self-titled eighth album arrives, fan-funded
years.p: They tour it with [[Into It. Over It.|d308cde9-0e44-4fe0-986d-e4657b6e8b7c]] and Hostage Calm. The same month, they play Through Being Cool front to back at a secret Brooklyn show.

years.h: Max Bemis does the math, and Through Being Cool turns 15 on tour
years.p: Saves the Day play Through Being Cool in full while [[Say Anything|ee90d1b3-a4e2-4d18-9092-111d856e7e7a]] play ...Is a Real Boy, with [[Reggie and the Full Effect|2bfce7d5-001d-4618-adc3-c57c30fb17e6]] doing Under the Tray.
years.xp: The idea came from Bemis, who noticed his record turned ten the same year Conley's turned fifteen. The tour was announced September 4 and ran November 14 to December 21, and Equal Vision reissued the album on vinyl. Earlier that year Saves the Day supported [[Brand New|9311e2bc-bb3f-44cf-90d8-b1fe6912b60b]] in the UK.

years.h: 9 arrives twenty years after Can't Slow Down
years.p: Announced with "Rendezvous" on August 14, Saves the Day's ninth record comes out on Equal Vision.

eras.title: Reckoning and return
eras.text: Claudio Rivera came back to the drums. In May 2021 a former fan accused Conley of sexual misconduct, and Conley answered with a public statement. By 2026 Saves the Day were supporting Taking Back Sunday on tour.

years.h: Claudio Rivera is back on the drum stool
years.p: Dennis Wilson leaves, and Rivera, who played from 2010 to 2013, rejoins.

years.h: Chris Conley is accused of sexual misconduct and says he caused harm
years.p: A former fan accuses him of sexual misconduct and abuse of power, including sending unsolicited nude photos. Conley admits to inappropriate missteps causing irreversible harm, and Equal Vision says it is looking into it.
years.xp: Conley's statement: "I am truly ashamed and embarrassed by my abhorrent behavior." Equal Vision said it was working to uncover what had happened.

years.h: Taking Back Sunday book Saves the Day for their fall tour
years.p: [[Thrice|244afcb7-fa9a-49b1-9aa6-0149512d1c52]] is also on the bill, announced April 28.

years.h: "Invader" brings in Walter Schreifels
years.p: Out September 9, the song features Schreifels of [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]] and [[Rival Schools|c661021c-3a9f-49d2-948a-c7f357cb1c87]].
